text:
alex kim: heads up — safety/snyk flagged CVE-2025-0421 in tokenizers 0.15.2 (wheel binary). CI started failing after yesterday's deps bump :exclamation:
Mira Patel: saw the failing build, looks like manylinux wheel shim error during install :confused:
Samir Gupta: can someone paste the pip/poetry error? i want to see which step breaks
alex kim: paste from CI log:
```
ERROR: Could not build wheels for tokenizers which use PEP 517 and cannot be installed directly
  running bdist_wheel
  error: command 'x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc' failed with exit status 1
```
Mira Patel: that's odd — tokenizers provides wheels normally. I suspect the buildhost image changed in base CI or a new build flag in the wheel. also Snyk reports the vuln in tokenizers' dependency chain (rust binding surface).
dependabot: Automated security update of tokenizers from 0.14.9 to 0.15.2 requested in PR #3821 :robot_face:
Samir Gupta: quick triage plan: 1) bisect the recent lockfile to find exact bump that introduced the bad wheel/flag, 2) try a local pip install of the wheel on the CI base image, 3) if wheel missing, pin a compatible tokenizers wheel or revert bump and backport fix.
alex kim: i started a local reproduce using the ubuntu:22.04 image and got the same gcc failure — looks like the wheel was not built for our platform. also Snyk shows a CVE with an upstream parsing bug in tokenizer's rust layer (low confidence exploitability for our usage).
Mira Patel: given exploitability is uncertain, we should treat as high if it's an upstream memory issue. mitigation options: patch tokenizers on our side (impossible), pin to previous safe version, or vendor a patched wheel.
Samir Gupta: propose: create a short-lived release branch (hotfix/tokenizers-cve-1769), cherry-pick the last known-good poetry.lock entry, regenerate lock, run full CI. If that passes, backport to release-2026.01. Also open an issue with the tokenizers maintainers and ask for a CVE advisory.
alex kim: +1. also request infra to run a new build matrix with musl/manylinux images — file an eng-infra ticket. @Mira can you start the hotfix branch? :clipboard:
Mira Patel: starting branch now. i'll pin tokenizers to 0.14.9 in pyproject.toml and run `poetry lock --no-update` then open PR with the lockfile and a short explanation.
Mira Patel: note — when i ran `poetry lock --no-update` locally, we still pulled in a transitive bump from transformers 4.35 -> 4.36 that changes a dependency. Samir, can you run a quick `git bisect` between the last green CI sha and current to find which package change triggered the new tokenizers wheel?
Samir Gupta: running bisect now, looks like the transformers bump pulled a new tokenizer pin in requirements via extras. bisect shows the transformers upgrade is the proximate cause.
alex kim: thanks. action items: - Mira: open PR pinning tokenizers and lockfile - Samir: prepare bisect notes and a minimal repro script for infra - sec-bot: run Snyk full scan on the pinned PR and label severity - dependabot: hold further automerged tokenizers PRs until hotfix merged
sec-bot: Snyk scan queued for PR #hotfix-tokenizers, expected results in ~15m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
dependabot: Holding further updates to tokenizers until manual review requested by repo admins.
Mira Patel: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/hotfix/tokenizers-cve-1769 — includes pinned tokenizers, regenerated poetry.lock, and a note to backport if CI green.
Samir Gupta: CI passed on hotfix branch except for one lint failure unrelated. Snyk scan reported the CVE but marked exploitability "low" for our runtime. Still want backport?
alex kim: backport anyway — we prefer conservative posture. release team, please schedule the backport to the next patch release window. also add an audit log entry documenting the transient pin and rationale (RBAC: only eng-security and release leads can approve).
Mira Patel: noted — i'll add audit log entry and tag release leads. also adding a follow-up to evaluate KMS client bump that was in same window — it touched build-time env vars and may have affected wheel builds.
Samir Gupta: created issue #4123 to track tokenizers upstream CVE, KMS client interaction, and a postmortem of how dep bumps landed on main without canary constraints.
alex kim: thanks team. once backport is merged let's remove the temporary pin and coordinate with model infra on a longer-term mitigation (cached vetted wheels or internal mirror). :thumbsup:
